title: Role schema harmonization and incremental switchover (RBAC v1 -> v2) with audit streaming
creator: Aisha Chen
description: Objective: harmonize the v1 and v2 role schemas, enable an incremental switchover path using dual-write + streaming audit events, and provide a safe canary rollout with automated reconciliation and clear rollback criteria. This ticket coordinates schema migration, SAML role mapping validation, admin UI locks, and audit log parity checks so customers experience no authorization regressions during migration.
acceptance_criteria: Dual-write enabled between v1 authoritative store and v2 authoritative store for role create/update/delete with <1s replication lag under normal load
Audit stream publishes change events (role assignments, admin actions, SSO mappings) to the central audit topic with event schema v2 and backwards-compatible fields
Canary cohort (10 internal orgs + 3 external pilot customers) successfully served by RBAC v2 with no auth regressions for 48h
Automated reconciliation job detects and repairs drift >0.1% within 15 minutes for primary index keys
Fallback switch to v1 authoritative decisions within 2 minutes when critical integrity or authorization errors are detected
Design doc, runbook, and customer communication templates linked and approved by Product & Security
implementation_plan: 1) Schema alignment: add v2-only columns and migration-safe defaults; introduce role fingerprint for idempotent reconciliation
2) Dual-write middleware: implement a write-side adapter that writes synchronous updates to both stores and emits an audit event; include short-lived tombstone markers for deletes
3) Audit streaming: standardize event envelope (event_type, timestamp, actor, source_version, role_fingerprint, prev_hash) and stream to kafka/audit-topic-v2
4) SAML role mapping verification: add a validation step in the SSO pipeline that simulates mapping against both stores and flags mismatches to a vetting dashboard
5) Admin UI safeguards: disable destructive role deletes for canary orgs; add a confirmation modal with diff view for role edits
6) Reconciliation agent: implement eventual backfill worker with priority queue, rate limits, and safe-merge semantics
7) Canary cutover: route auth decisions for pilot organizations to v2 decision path while keeping v1 as fallback
8) Observability: add traces, metrics (replication_lag_ms, reconciliation_drift_rate, auth_errors_by_store), and pre-defined alerts
9) Docs & runbooks: finalize playbook for on-call, rollback steps, and customer escalation paths
rollout_plan: Phase A (internal): enable dual-write + audit stream for internal orgs and run reconciliation with aggressive thresholds for 72h
Phase B (pilot): invite 3 opt-in external customers representing different roles models; monitor for 7 days; daily sync calls
Phase C (wave 1): open to low-risk customers (no cross-account role delegation) in batches of 200 orgs/day with automated health checks
Phase D (full): if waves stable for 5 days, enable dual-write as default and begin scheduled unilateral reads from v2 for read-mostly traffic; retention of v1 for 90 days for emergency fallback
Communication: pre-rollout notice (7d), pilot onboarding docs, in-console banner for affected orgs, and post-rollout confirmation email
monitoring_and_rollback: Live metrics to watch: auth_denial_increase_pct, replication_lag_p95, audit_event_missing_rate, reconciliation_throughput, saml_mapping_mismatch_rate
Alert thresholds: auth_denial_increase_pct > 3% sustained for 10m => P0 incident; replication_lag_p95 > 1500ms => P1; audit_event_missing_rate > 0.5% => P0
Automated rollback: trigger a controlled switch of decision routing back to v1 for affected org IDs when P0 alert fires; maintain dual-write but pause v2 reads
Manual rollback: follow runbook steps to rehydrate v1 authoritative index from audit stream snapshots if divergence detected >1%
Post-incident analysis: postmortem within 72h and update reconciliation heuristics
notes_and_decisions: Decision: v2 will be the long-term authoritative store; during migration we keep v1 writable to preserve customer safety
Decision: use fingerprint + prev_hash in audit events to detect silent concurrent edits across stores
Trade-off: synchronous dual-write increases tail latency by ~20ms — acceptable for mutation paths given safety benefits
Trade-off: reconciliation worker may produce transient permission expansions during repair — restrict repair to additive permissions first and run conservative merges for removes
Open question: whether to block third-party SCIM syncs during pilot; current plan is to flag and notify but not block
